title: Logging and crash reports to a local file
when: Users report bugs in the desktop app and nobody can see what happened; the app needs local logs and a crash report the user can choose to send.
prompt:
Goal: log.js writes leveled, rotated log lines to the user data folder, and unexpected errors produce a local crash report the user can review and share.
Steps:
1. Log path: (await Neutralino.os.getPath("data")) + "/NotesDesk/logs/app.log".
2. Line format: ISO time, level (debug, info, warn, error), area, message, as one JSON object per line.
3. Buffer lines and append every 2 seconds with Neutralino.filesystem.appendFile; flush on windowClose.
4. Rotate at 1 MB: rename app.log to app.1.log, keep 3 files.
5. Catch crashes: window.addEventListener("error") and ("unhandledrejection") write an error entry with stack, app version (NL_VERSION), OS (NL_OS) and the last 50 log lines into crash-<time>.json.
6. Redact: never log file contents, tokens, emails or full paths under the home folder; replace with "<redacted>" or "~".
7. On the next start, if a new crash file exists, show "The app closed unexpectedly. Open report?" with Open folder and Dismiss; sending is the user choice.
8. Neutralinojs native logs go to neutralinojs.log when the logging block is enabled in the config; mention both files in Help.
Quality bar:
- Logs never grow without limit.
- Nothing personal leaves the machine without consent.
Pitfalls:
- Writing a file on every log call, which slows the UI.
- Logging in the install folder.
Verify:
- [ ] Rotation keeps at most 3 files.
- [ ] error and unhandledrejection are captured.
- [ ] Redaction runs before writing.
Output: log.js, crash.js and a Help section on finding logs.

examples.input: cliente diz que o app desktop fecha sozinho e eu não sei por que
examples.output: JSON lines log in data folder, 1 MB rotation, crash file with last 50 lines, redaction, open report prompt
